p1.title: How to Choose the Right Fire Protection Company for Your Project (And Avoid Amateurs)
p1.excerpt: The safety market is full of companies. How do you distinguish between a certified expert and an amateur? Your guide to avoiding unqualified vendors.
p1.content:
1. Verify Official Certification

The first and most important step is ensuring the company is certified by the Civil Defense. Do not rely on verbal confirmation; ask to see the certificate and check its expiration date.

2. Documented Track Record

Ask for a list of similar projects the company has executed. Have they handled projects of the same size and complexity? Contacting previous clients can provide real insights into work quality and commitment.

3. Qualified Technical Team

Does the company have certified engineers and technicians? Modern systems require high technical expertise for installation and programming. Untrained labor can cause future disasters.

4. After-Sales & Maintenance

Your relationship with the company doesn't end after installation. Ensure they have a strong maintenance department and rapid emergency response.

5. Clear Contract & Pricing

The contract must be detailed, covering all items and specifications. Avoid vague contracts that may hide additional costs later.

p2.title: How to Read a Quote? (Your Guide to Analyzing Offers & Spotting Hidden Items)
p2.excerpt: Received an offer for 50k and another for 35k? Is cheaper always better? Learn how to uncover the trick of estimated quantities.
p2.content:
Don't Be Fooled by the Final Number

Comparing quotes based solely on the final price is the biggest mistake facility owners make. You must analyze the offer item by item.

The 'Estimated Quantities' Trick

Some companies list fewer quantities than required to appear cheaper, then charge you the difference during execution (Variation Order). Ensure quantities are 'Lump Sum' or based on an approved plan.

Material Specifications (Brand List)

Ensure the brand and origin of each item are specified. A European fire pump differs in price and quality from a Chinese one.

Payment & Warranty Terms

The payment schedule must be tied to actual progress. Don't forget warranty terms: Does it cover spare parts? For how long?

p3.title: Checklist: Is Your System Compliant with Civil Defense Requirements?
p3.excerpt: Inspector visiting tomorrow? We've prepared a quick checklist (documents, exits, equipment) so you can verify compliance beforehand.
p3.content:
1. Documents & Records

  • Building Permit and Building Completion Certificate.
  • Valid, electronically documented maintenance contract.
  • Technical report from a certified engineering office (if applicable).

2. Firefighting & Alarm Systems

  • Alarm panel is operational with No Faults.
  • Fire pumps are in Auto Mode.
  • Fire hoses are intact and properly folded.
  • Fire extinguishers are in place, pressure gauge in the green zone.

3. Emergency Exits

  • Exits are unlocked and clear of obstacles.
  • 'EXIT' signs are illuminated and working.
  • Emergency doors open outwards and have a Panic Bar.

p4.title: The Comprehensive Guide to Issuing a 'Civil Defense License' via Salama Portal (2025)
p4.excerpt: From registration to printing. Learn the difference between instant and non-instant licenses, and how to avoid processing delays.
p4.content:
Instant vs. Non-Instant Licenses

Instant licenses are issued for low-risk, small-area activities immediately after contracting a safety company. Non-instant licenses require a field visit.

Issuance Steps via Salama Portal

  1. Log in and select 'Issue New License'.
  2. Accurately enter facility data and activity type.
  3. Select a certified safety company to provide the technical report and maintenance contract.
  4. Pay the required fees.
  5. The safety company uploads the report and approves it via the system.
  6. Print the license instantly (if instant) or await the visit.

Common Errors Causing Delays

Choosing the wrong activity, unpaid previous violations, or expired company CR. Ensure all paperwork is valid before starting.

p5.title: The 'Technical Report' in Balady: When Does Civil Defense Request It?
p5.excerpt: Why is a technical report requested for old buildings or activity changes? Ensure first-time approval via a certified office.
p5.content:
What is a Technical Report?

An engineering document proving the building is structurally and electrically safe and complies with the Saudi Building Code. Requested by Civil Defense in specific cases.

When is it Requested?

  • Renewing a license for an old building without a completion certificate.
  • Changing the facility's activity (e.g., from retail to restaurant).
  • Structural modifications or building expansions.

How to Ensure Approval?

It must be prepared by an approved, classified engineering office. It should include plans, photos, and test results proving compliance.

p6.title: Electrical Installation Safety Certificate: Invisible Protection
p6.excerpt: Electrical short circuits are the leading cause of fires. Discover the importance of electrical safety certificates for factories.
p6.content:
Why is it Important?

Most fires start due to electrical faults (shorts, overloads, poor connections). This certificate ensures your electrical network is safe and compliant.

What Does the Engineer Check?

  • Cable and breaker Load Balancing.
  • Earthing System integrity.
  • Wire insulation and connection quality.
  • Testing Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers (ELCB).

Who Needs It?

Mandatory for factories, warehouses, and high-risk buildings. It is a prerequisite for license renewal and insurance.

p7.title: Installation Completion Certificate: Requirements & Releasing Power
p7.excerpt: For new buildings, the electric company requires this certificate. Learn about the pressure and pump tests required for issuance.
p7.content:
What is the Completion Certificate?

A declaration by a certified contractor and consultant that all safety systems are successfully installed, tested, and operational. Without it, power won't be released to new buildings.

Required Tests for Issuance

  • Hydrostatic Test for pipe networks to ensure no leaks.
  • Pump Performance Curve tests at various flows.
  • Alarm system testing and its integration with elevators and HVAC.

Important Advice

Do not postpone these tests to the last minute. Conduct them in phases during execution to avoid breaking walls/ceilings later.

p8.title: Electronic Maintenance Contracts: Guide to Avoiding Non-Renewal Fines
p8.excerpt: Maintenance contracts are now electronic and linked to Salama. How to choose the right contract and ensure emergency response.
p8.content:
Digital Transformation of Contracts

Paper contracts are no longer sufficient. Contracts must be registered in the 'Salama' portal and linked to your facility's license.

What Should the Contract Include?

  • Number of periodic visits (monthly or quarterly).
  • Emergency response time (e.g., within 4 hours).
  • Provision of authentic spare parts (Are they included?).

Avoid Fake Contracts

Contracting a company just to 'renew the license' without real maintenance exposes you to severe risks, fines, and license cancellation in case of an incident.

p9.title: Water Sprinklers vs. FM200: How to Choose the Right System?
p9.excerpt: Should I install water sprinklers because they are cheaper? The SBC has the answer. A technical comparison between water and gas.
p9.content:
Water Sprinkler System

Pros: Low cost, readily available extinguishing agent, highly effective at controlling fires.

Cons: Causes property damage (papers, electronics) upon activation.

Usage: Warehouses, offices, malls, garages.

Clean Gas System (FM200 / NOVEC)

Pros: Extinguishes fires in seconds, leaves no residue, completely safe for sensitive electronics.

Cons: Very high cost, requires an airtight room.

Usage: Server rooms (Data Centers), electrical rooms, important archives, museums.

Conclusion

Don't skimp on protecting a server room with water, and don't waste money installing gas in an open warehouse. Every risk has a tailored system.

p10.title: Restaurant Guide: Wet Chemical Fire Suppression Requirements
p10.excerpt: Civil Defense requires this system to license any restaurant. Learn its mandatory components and the importance of the gas shut-off valve.
p10.content:
Why Wet Chemical?

Cooking oil fires (Class K) cannot be extinguished with water or dry powder; they may flare up. Wet Chemical reacts with oil to form a soapy foam layer, blocking oxygen and cooling the oil.

Mandatory System Components

  • Chemical cylinder (sized according to hood volume).
  • Pipe network and nozzles precisely aimed at cooking zones.
  • Fusible Links inside the hood that melt at specific temperatures to activate the system.
  • Gas Shut-off Valve: The most crucial part; cuts off gas instantly during a fire to prevent feeding the flames.

Maintenance

Cooking grease accumulates on detectors and nozzles. Routine cleaning and maintenance are a matter of life and death in restaurants.
